# Clipper

**Hard to Soft Clipper with a Live Transfer Curve**

A VST3 distortion effect for Windows. One shaping function drives both the audio and the
display, so the curve on screen is literally the curve the samples pass through. Written in
C++20 on JUCE.

![Clipper main window](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ClyntiaAikaHanaa/Clipper/HEAD/Screenshot/Main.png)

## What it does

Clipping is the bluntest tool in the mixing box and still one of the most used: cut the
peaks, get the loudness back, and pick up some harmonics on the way. Most clippers either
hide the shape behind a single drive knob or draw a curve that is only a rough sketch of
what the DSP is doing.

Clipper shows the real thing. The transfer function you drag is the function the audio
thread calls, sample for sample, and the waveform behind it is the actual output of the
plugin rather than a redrawn approximation.

Three things shape the design:

1. **One shaping function, two consumers.** `clipper::dsp::clip()` is header only and free
   of JUCE types, so the audio thread and the display call the same code. The picture and
   the sound cannot drift apart.
2. **The ceiling is a guarantee.** Oversampled clipping alone leaves ripple and a few
   percent of overshoot past the threshold once the signal is filtered back down. A second
   clamp at the base rate restores the flat tops and makes the ceiling real.
3. **Small on purpose.** Four parameters, one window, no preset browser. It is meant to be
   dropped on a bus and set in ten seconds.

## Features

### Engine

* Piecewise quadratic knee, chosen so that knee at 0 percent is exactly hard clipping with
  no special case, unity slope is kept until the signal approaches the ceiling, and the
  curve reaches the ceiling at a finite input instead of only asymptotically.
* C1 continuous at both joins, so nothing kinks audibly as the signal crosses into the knee.
* 2x oversampling around the shaping stage using the polyphase IIR half band pair. That is
  a minimum phase filter, so latency stays a fraction of a sample instead of the dozens a
  linear phase FIR would cost, and whatever it does report is forwarded to the host so
  delay compensation stays correct.
* Base rate clamp after downsampling, which flattens the tops the reconstruction filter
  rounded off and stops peaks landing above the ceiling the user set.
* All four controls smoothed over 5 ms at the oversampled rate, so a hard automation jump
  cannot click.
* Denormals disabled on the audio thread, so a long silence costs nothing.

### Controls

| Control | Range | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| In Gain | -24 to +24 dB | Level going into the clipper. More drive, more distortion. |
| Knee | 0 to 100 percent | Shape of the clip, from a hard corner to a soft rounded knee. |
| Out Gain | -24 to +24 dB | Level after clipping, for matching the loudness back. |
| Ceiling | -24 to 0 dB | How far the signal is allowed to go. Dragged from the display. |

### Display

* Transfer curve sampled once per pixel, so the knee stays smooth at any window size.
* Live output waveform behind the curve, drawn on the same vertical scale, so the ceiling
  rules land exactly where the trace is being flattened.
* Bins the clipper is currently holding are picked out brighter, so the moment the signal
  starts squaring off is visible rather than inferred.
* Two triangle markers set the ceiling by dragging. Double click either one to return it to
  full scale.
* The plot covers the clipping stage only. Out Gain is a separate stage after it and
  deliberately does not move anything in the panel, so the markers stay put and a drag
  lands on the value under the cursor.
* Status bar describes whatever is under the mouse.

### Interface

* Resizable from 70 percent to 250 percent by dragging the bottom right corner.
* The aspect ratio is locked and the whole panel is drawn at its design size and scaled by
  a single transform, so every knob, arc, glyph and caption keeps its exact proportion at
  any size. No control carries a size or DPI branch of its own.
* The window size is stored with the project, so the editor reopens where it was left.
* Double click any knob to return it to its default.

## Project layout

```
Source/
  ClipperDSP.h      the shaping function, shared by the audio thread and the display
  Params.*          parameter IDs, ranges, formatting and status bar copy
  PluginProcessor.* oversampling, gain staging, output scope, state
  PluginEditor.*    resizable shell, single transform scaling
  MainPanel.*       title bar, layout, status bar
  CurveDisplay.*    transfer curve, output waveform, ceiling handles
  Widgets.h         arc knob and the brand mark
  ClipperTheme.h    palette, fonts and shared dimensions
Tools/
  logoexport.cpp    brand asset export
Screenshot/
  Main.png
  Logo.png
  make_logo.ps1
```

Clipper shares its palette and layout language with the rest of the series, so it sits at
the same size on screen and reads as the same family.
